paper.title: Quantum Entanglement Path Selection and Qubit Allocation via Adversarial Group Neural Bandits

unmapped: Arms are partitioned into R groups (paths); each group r has an unknown nonlinear reward function h_r in [0,1] on D_r-dimensional arms, learned via overparameterized neural networks (NTK)
Adversary chooses a binary attack vector a^t over groups each round; reward success rate s^t = a^t(r) h_r(x), observed outcome Y^t ~ Bernoulli(s^t); attacks are distinguishable from failures
Comparator: best fixed group in hindsight, playing the per-round optimal arm within that group (group-static strategies)
settings.definition_quote: the adversary simultaneously chooses a binary attack vector $a^t = (a^t(r), \forall r\in \mathcal{R})$, where $a^t (r) = 0$ if the adversary performs an attack on the path $r$ and $a^t(r)=1$ otherwise. ... $\reg(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T s^t(\gamma, \xi_\gamma^t) - \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T s^t(r^t, x^t)]$

conditions: 0 <= h_r(x) <= 1 for all groups r and arms x
network width m >= poly(T, L, max_r D_r, 1/lambda, log(1/delta)) (sufficiently large)

source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0, 1)$, by choosing $\beta = T^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log(T)}$ and $\eta = T^{-1/2}$, such that for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, if $m, \lambda, \zeta$ satisfy the same condition as Lemma 2, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, EXPNeuralUCB yields the following expected regret bound $\reg(T) = O(T^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(T)})$.

results.notes: Regret is defined via success rates (means) against the best fixed group with per-round optimal arm; expectation over algorithm randomness, probability 1-delta over NN init/noise. Hidden dependence on effective dimension d_tilde, number of groups R and m^{-1/6} terms suppressed in the O. Comparator mapped to best_fixed_action (best fixed group). Adversary type (oblivious/adaptive) not specified in the theorem.
